extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system (mathematicians and computational algebraists) who use the arr.lib, customstd.lib, and phindex.lib libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (primarily arr.lib for hyperplane/multi-arrangements, plus customstd.lib and phindex.lib). Describes usage, return values, notes and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrLocalize
rubrics_metrics.description: arrLocalize(A, v); arrangement A, intvec v. Return: arr: the localized arrangement A^X, i.e. A^X only contains the hyperplanes which contain the flat X, which is defined by the equations A[v].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown; notes that this is from arr.lib. See also related procedures arrCone, arrDecone, arrEssentialize, arrIsEssential, arrRestrict.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrRestrict
rubrics_metrics.description: arrRestrict(A, v[, CC]); Return: arr: the restricted hyperplane arrangement A^X. Restriction is performed only if the ideal defining the flat X (A[v]) is monomial (i.e. X is an intersection of coordinate planes). If optional argument CC is given, the arrangement is transformed so X has that monomial form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty. Examples show usage with single index and intvec; demonstrates transformation when 'CC' is provided. See also related arr.* functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrIsEssential
rubrics_metrics.description: arrIsEssential(A); Return: boolean: 1 if arr is essential, i.e. rank of maximal element of poset equals dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty. Examples show return 1 or 0 for sample arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrEssentialize
rubrics_metrics.description: arrEssentialize(A); Return: essential arrangement by transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty. Examples show how a non-essential arrangement is transformed into an essential one. See also arrIsEssential.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrBoolean
rubrics_metrics.description: arrBoolean(v); int v. Return: arr, which uses the first v variables of ring for boolean arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates arrBoolean(7) producing hyperplanes corresponding to x(1)..x(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: arrBraid
rubrics_metrics.description: arrBraid(v); int v. Return: Type A (braid) arrangement of dimension v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lists the pairwise differences x(i)-x(j) for braid arrangement; typical use for symmetric-group hyperplane arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrTypeB
rubrics_metrics.description: arrTypeB(v); int v. Return: arrangement using first v variables for reflection arrangement of type B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows hyperplanes x(i)-x(j), x(i)+x(j), and coordinate hyperplanes x(i). See also arrTypeD and other predefined types.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrTypeD
rubrics_metrics.description: arrTypeD(v); int v. Return: arrangement using first v variables for reflection arrangement of type D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lists hyperplanes for type D (x(i)-x(j), x(i)+x(j) without coordinate hyperplanes).

rubrics_metrics.name: arrRandom
rubrics_metrics.description: arrRandom(n,v,N); int n,v,N. Return: Random arrangement where m is the number of hyperplanes, n the dimension, d (or N) is the upper bound for absolute value of coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: can also write arr = random(d,m,n) to create random arrangements. Example shows produced linear forms with integer coefficients bounded as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrRandomCentral
rubrics_metrics.description: arrRandomCentral(d,m,n); int d,m,n. Return: Random central arrangement where m is number of hyperplanes, n the dimension, d the upper bound for absolute value of coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows central (no constant term) hyperplane equations. Same parameter semantics as arrRandom but for central arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrEdelmanReiner
rubrics_metrics.description: arrEdelmanReiner(); Return: the Edelman–Reiner arrangement, a specific arrangement that is free but whose restriction to the 6th hyperplane is nonfree (counterexample to Orlik conjecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: active ring must have at least five variables. Example prints the 21 hyperplanes of this special arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrOrlikSolomon
rubrics_metrics.description: arrOrlikSolomon(A); arr A. Return: [ring] exterior Algebra E as ring with Orlik–Solomon ideal as attribute I. The Orlik–Solomon ideal is generated by differentials of dependent tuples of hyperplanes; for complex arrangements E/I is isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access ideal I activate this exterior algebra with setring. Example shows generators of the Orlik–Solomon ideal for arrTypeB(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: arrDer
rubrics_metrics.description: arrDer(A); arr A or multarr A. Return: [module] The module Der(A) of derivations of the (multi-)arrangement A, i.e. derivations tangent to each hyperplane of A (resp. with multiplicities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined only for central (multi-)arrangements. Examples show derivation modules for Boolean, Braid and generic arrangements. See arrIsFree and arrExponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrIsFree
rubrics_metrics.description: arrIsFree(A); arr A or multarr A. Return: [0,1] 1 if the (multi-)arrangement is free, i.e. Der(A) is a free module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only defined for central arrangements. Examples: Boolean and Type B arrangements return 1, generic arrangement returns 0. See arrDer and arrExponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrExponents
rubrics_metrics.description: arrExponents(A); arr A or multarr A. Return: [intvec] The exponents of a free (multi-)arrangement, i.e. the degrees of a basis of D(A), the derivation module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only defined for central arrangements. Example: arrExponents(Boolean3) -> 1,1,1; arrExponents(B3) -> 1,3,5. See arrDer and arrIsFree.

rubrics_metrics.name: arr2multarr (multArrFromIntvec)
rubrics_metrics.description: multArrFromIntvec(arr A, intvec v); Return: [multarr] multiarrangement MA, which is arrangement A with multiplicities v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size of v must match the number of hyperplanes in A. Example shows turning arrTypeB(3) into a multarrangement with all multiplicities 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: multarr2arr
rubrics_metrics.description: multarr2arr(multarr A, intvec v); Return: [arr] arrangement A with all multiplicities removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example converts a multarrangement with powers (x)^2, (y)^3, (z)^5 back to plain arrangement x,y,z.

rubrics_metrics.name: multarrRestrict
rubrics_metrics.description: multarrRestrict(A, v[, CC]); Return: [multarr] the restricted hyperplane Multi-Arrangement (A^X) with multiplicities, counting how often each element of the restricted arrangement occurs as intersection of hyperplanes of the first arrangement (definition due to G. M. Ziegler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty. Restriction only performed if ideal defining flat X is monomial; optional 'CC' transforms arrangement so X is an intersection of coordinate planes. Example demonstrates resulting multiplicities and transformed linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: multarrMultRestrict
rubrics_metrics.description: multarrMultRestrict(A, k); multiarrangement A, integer k. Return: [multarr] the restricted hyperplane Multi-Arrangement (A^{H_k}) with multiplicities, counting with multiplicities how often one element of restricted arrangement occurs as intersection of hyperplane of the first multiarrangement (Ziegler's definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A must be non-empty. Restriction only performed if H_k = ker(x_i) for some i; otherwise a coordinate change is required (use arrCoordchange) because such coordinate changes are not unique. Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrFlats
rubrics_metrics.description: arrFlats(A); usage shown as size(A); Return: [arrposet] Intersection lattice of an arrangement (poset of flats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example arrFlats(arrBraid(5)) prints computing messages, expected/executed ops, cleaned hyperplanes and then the poset grouped by rank with lists of flats. Useful for debugging and inspection of intersection lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: arrLattice(arr ARR); Return: [arrposet] intersection poset of the arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm works bottom-up. Example prints matrix tests and corresponding poset by ranks. See arrFlats for related output.

rubrics_metrics.name: moebius
rubrics_metrics.description: moebius(arrposet P); Return: [arrposet] fills in the Möbius values of the flats in the poset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows that initially Möbius values are uninitialized (placeholders) and calling P=moebius(P) initializes them; printMoebius can display values.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrCharPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: arrCharPoly(arr A); Return: [intvec] coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of A in increasing order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: algorithm returns coefficients only (integers) though base ring could be different. Example with arrBraid(5) demonstrates polynomial and returned vector (24,-50,35,-10,1 corresponding to coefficients).

rubrics_metrics.name: arrPoincare
rubrics_metrics.description: arrPoincare(A); arr A. Return: [intvec] The Poincaré polynomial as integer vector of the arrangement, equal to the second-kind Poincaré series of the Orlik–Solomon algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: arrPoincare(arrBraid(5)) returns vector [1,10,35,50,24] corresponding to polynomial expansion (1+x)(1+2x)(1+3x)(1+4x). See arrChambers, arrBoundedChambers.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrChambers
rubrics_metrics.description: arrChambers(A); arr A. Return: [int] The number of chambers of an arrangement, equal to evaluation of Poincaré polynomial at 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: arrChambers(ideal(x,y,x+y-1)) -> 7. See arrPoincare and arrBoundedChambers.

rubrics_metrics.name: arrBoundedChambers
rubrics_metrics.description: arrBoundedChambers(A); arr A. Return: [int] The number of bounded chambers of an arrangement, equal to evaluation of Poincaré polynomial at -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: arrBoundedChambers(ideal(x,y,x+y-1)) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: printMoebius
rubrics_metrics.description: printMoebius(A); arrposet A. Return: [] displays the Möbius values of all the flats in the poset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly used for debugging. Example shows pre- and post-moebius values and usage with arrBraid(4) lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: monomialabortstd
rubrics_metrics.description: monomialabortstd(I); I ideal. Purpose: computes a standard basis and aborts if a monomial generator is found. Returns all standard-basis elements that have been computed up to the abort point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to sequencing of algorithm: if aborted, there is no guarantee monomial found is final standard-basis element; if ideal has a monomial generator, computation may not necessarily abort initially. Examples illustrate normal behavior, immediate return when a generator is monomial, and that the monomial causing the abort may not be final basis element.

rubrics_metrics.name: satstd
rubrics_metrics.description: satstd(I[,J]); I ideal, J optional ideal (assumed generated by variables). Purpose: computes a standard basis of I and, if possible, divides each polynomial during computation by variables in J. By default J is the ideal generated by all variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is a standard basis of the saturation with respect to the product of variables in J. Note that even if I contains a monomial generated by variables in J, it may not be found during computation; if found, 1 is immediately returned. Examples show differences when saturating wrt a variable, and effect on degree bound of standard basis of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureL
rubrics_metrics.description: signatureL(M[,r]); M symmetric matrix, optional int r. Return: signature of M (an int) or if r is given and !=0 then intvec (signature, number of +, number of -).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: constructs quadratic form associated to M and uses Lagrange method to compute signature. Explains law of inertia: rank r = pi + nu, signature s = pi - nu. References Gantmacher. Examples show usage and returned signature vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureLqf
rubrics_metrics.description: signatureLqf(h); h quadratic form (polynomial). Return: signature of h as int or intvec (signature, nr of +, nr of -) if optional r-like behavior is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses method of Lagrange to reduce quadratic form to sum of squares; same theoretical background as signatureL. Intended to compute signature from polynomial quadratic form. Example placeholder indicated.
